title: Tanzanian Grilled Tilapia
community: Beloved around Lake Victoria and across mainland Tanzania
author: Chef Jabir
desc: Tanzanian Grilled Tilapia — fresh whole tilapia scored and seasoned with lemon, garlic, and spices, grilled over charcoal until the skin is crispy and the flesh is moist and flaky. The fish dish of Lake Victoria — Tanzania's most eaten freshwater fish.
longDesc: Tilapia (sato) is the fish of Lake Victoria and inland Tanzania — abundant, affordable, and extraordinarily versatile. Grilled with the simplest seasoning, it is the lakeside fish dish that millions of Tanzanians eat weekly.
ingredients: 4 whole tilapia (400—500g each) — scaled and gutted
steps: Score fish 4—5 times on each side through to the bone.
Mix marinade. Rub all over fish and into scores. Marinate 30 minutes.
Grill over medium-high coals for 8—10 minutes per side.
Do not move until skin releases cleanly.
chefTips: Oil the grill before adding fish.
Do not move fish before skin releases.
cookingScience: Scoring through the skin prevents the skin from contracting and curling the fish, and allows marinade to penetrate the muscle fibres beneath.
sustainabilityTips: Lake Victoria tilapia supports millions of Tanzanian fishing families.
culturalNote: Grilled tilapia is the food of Lake Victoria — eaten at lakeside restaurants in Mwanza and Bukoba, always with ugali and kachumbari.
